item.title: [6.8] ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves...

WHY IT MATTERS

ZeroVLN presents a novel approach to vision-language navigation by avoiding SFT of the VLM brain through a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop RL.

item.title: [6.7] HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a...

WHY IT MATTERS

HiUni presents a technically sound approach to unifying visual understanding and generation using shared backbones, addressing a key architectural limitation in current multimodal models.
